issue_context.title: mgmg/mcumg/lib: Replace TinyCBOR with zcbor
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Trying to set on using single CBOR implementation within Zephyr.
Mcuboot has already switched from TinyCBOR (Zephyr specific fork) to zcbor.
This should also allow us to reset TinyCBOR fork to vanilla TinyCBOR from Intel (https://github.com/intel/tinycbor) as current TinyCBOR within Zephyr (https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/tinycbor) has been extracted fro Mynewt core (https://github.com/apache/mynewt-core/tree/master/encoding/tinycbor) and is not 100% compatible with Intel implementation.
The zcboris quite API compatible with TinyCBOR so the task should not be that time consuming.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Get rid of cborattr and move mcumgr to use zcbor. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
 1) Using zcbor:
     Against: not so widespread;
     For: it allows to generate decoding from frame descriptions in zcbor format; it is already used in mcboot; using single implementation saves flash for code;
 2) Using TinyCBOR in all Zephyr applications
     Against: mcuboot has already switched to the zbor and has been able to free some flash; more than one implementation of the same thing;
     For: this is kinda standard with many forks and used by 3rd party libraries
 3) Resetting mcumgr to Intel TinyCBOR:
    This is like 2) except that we use standard implementation.

**Additional context**
Intel TinyCBOR: https://github.com/intel/tinycbor
Zephyr TinyCBOR: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/tinycbor
zcbor: https://github.com/NordicSemiconductor/zcbor/
comments: I'll work on the OS group

review_comments: This is where I see a potential issue, if there has been some sensitive data pushed on the stack and the underlying data in `value` happens to have valid-ish data, some/all of that sensitive data might be returned to this command
As above, value isn't sure to be set if it wasn't included in the cbor map and will have undefined data

The way I see this is: `struct zcbor_string value;` value is undefined, `while()` loop processes all items in message, assuming that the message does contain valid data but no "name" tag and instead is "timber", `ok` will be true but `value` will never be set and will be undefined, so at this point `value.len` and `value.value` could be anything
`ok` is a bool and `zcbor_map_decode_bulk` is returning an int, is a cast needed?

I guess when I first heard of the proposal to move to zcbor, I was under the impression that it would be moving everything to a .cddl file and generating an input/output decoder with zcbor. Is that the long term goal or is the plan to keep with this style of encoding?

Nope. Encoding via CDDL wouldn't make sense, the code would get larger. The decoding has been planned to be moved to CDDL, but as the CDDL right now does not support decoding of payload where position of fields changes it is postponed.
The significant improvement though is that zcbor uses zcbor_string to point where data is placed in decoded buffer, for example the mcumgr buffer, which means that it is no longer needed to copy for example chunks of file image update to additional buffer, mcumgr transport buffer is used directly. This saves on stack an static variables, and copy operations.
Some Kconfig options will disappear.
